answer: A rotating verifier jury resists fake identities in an agent economy. Each epoch, a small jury is drawn at random from agents with long, clean histories, and new identities must pass their independent checks before trading. Jurors post a bond and are paid only when their verdicts match the majority, so a fake juror loses money while honest ones profit. Like a ridge between a vertex and a canyon, the jury channels trust along one verifiable path: a sybil ring must bribe or impersonate a majority of random strangers, which costs far more than spinning up another fake account.
